South Africa not only made India toil through 151.1 overs, but also took valuable time out of the game. With the hosts trailing in the series, the onus is firmly on them to force a result here in Guwahati. The Proteas have batted for nearly two full days, and it will take something special for India to swing this Test in their favour. Play can be extended by half an hour to make up overs, but given how quickly the light fades in Guwahati, it is unlikely we will get more than 30 minutes beyond the scheduled close. To add to that, it is overcast today, and it already looks darker than it did at this time yesterday. A tricky phase awaits the Indian openers. Back in a bit for the start of India's reply.

End of a solid batting effort from South Africa. First innings totals are always crucial and this is a job well done from the Proteas. The story of their top six batters was them getting starts but converting and at 246/6, they were in danger of being folded under 300. The lower order came to the rescue with the last 4 wickets adding 243 runs. Senuran Muthusamy led the charge with a superb maiden Test ton, stitching together valuable stands that made India grind hard. Marco Jansen made his intentions clear from the moment he walked in, shifting the tempo straightaway. Jansen kept going after Muthusamy perished and found an able ally in Maharaj, but he could not get to his hundred.

OUT! DRAGGED ON! Marco Jansen is absolutely distraught! Jansen falls 7 runs short of what would have been his maiden Test ton. Googly from Kuldeep, short and turning away from the batter. Marco hangs back and steers it behind square on the off side with an angled bat. Gets an inside edge that crashes back into the stumps. End of a marathon batting effort from South Africa as they finish with 489.

It was pretty much a chanceless partnership until an error by Verreynne led to his downfall. Marco Jansen's arrival saw the scoring rate pick up with the lanky speedster using his long levers to find the fence. Muthusamy got in on the act soon after and brought up his maiden Test ton. As the partnership grew, the Indian shoulders began to drop, and they just went through the motions for the remainder of the session. The Proteas have so far made the most of the good batting conditions and will be hungry for more when they return after the break, while India will have to find a way to take the remaining 3 wickets. Join us back at 2 pm IST (8.30 am GMT) for the post-Lunch session.

SESSION SUMMARY - 26 overs, 112 runs and 1 wicket. A dominant session for South Africa and an equally frustrating one for India. From being 246/6, this has been an extraordinary effort from the Proteas. Senuran Muthusamy and Kyle Verreynne carried on the good work for the touring side after the break. Just as was the case in the morning, they were happy to not try anything fancy and knuckled down. Not taking anything away from the Proteas pair, but the Indian spinners bowled a bit too fast and did not vary their speeds enough to challenge the batters.

Rishabh Pant leads his men out on the park. Mohammed Siraj has one ball left in his over. Senuran Muthusamy to face. Two slips and a gully in place. Let's play...

PITCH REPORT - Shaun Pollock is pitchside and notes that the surface looks noticeably drier today. He mentions that there was some moisture around yesterday, which helped produce movement for the pacers, and it also resulted in more bounce for the spinners in the morning session. He feels this might be a new-ball wicket, so it will be interesting to see what the second new ball does. Deep Dasgupta agrees that the surface has dried out and is starting to get a touch dusty. He points out developing footmarks that could offer a little more for the spinners as the day goes on. That said, he believes it remains a good batting wicket heading into Day 2.

As for India, they will be pleased with their collective effort. Their spinners did the bulk of the work on a surface that settled down as the day progressed, and their discipline shone through with tight lines and fields that forced the visitors to take risks. Looking ahead, with the second new ball less than two overs old, India will turn to Jasprit Bumrah and Mohammed Siraj, who, after a good night’s rest, will be raring to limit the South African total and set the tone early on Day 2. Stay tuned for all the action.

After the toss fell South Africa’s way, Temba Bavuma had no hesitation in batting first. All four of their top-order batters looked to have settled in, with each facing at least 80 balls, but none converted, giving their wickets away after doing the hard work. The story was similar for Tony de Zorzi, who fell late in the day to the second new ball. Their hopes now rest on Senuran Muthusamy and Kyle Verreynne, and even the three to come are no mugs with the bat as they look to stretch the total closer to 300.

Hello and a warm welcome, everyone! Barsapara Cricket Stadium’s first day as a Test venue brought serenity after all the chaos and fast-forward pace of Kolkata. It was back to the old-fashioned rhythm of Test cricket, where patience, discipline, and attrition took centre stage. India would have been the slightly happier of the two sides at stumps, whereas for South Africa, although they managed to put up 247, it is the wickets column that will sting.

So, as Tristan Stubbs has said, they are a bit disappointed that everyone in the top six got starts, but none could anchor the innings. South Africa still have four wickets in hand but with the second new ball just 1.3 overs old, India will look to make early inroads tomorrow. Join us for the action of Day 2 at 9 am IST (3.30 am GMT). Till then, cheers!

Tristan Stubbs is in for a chat. He says he is a bit disappointed because everyone in the top six got starts, but none could kick on and make it big. Adds that he enjoys batting at number three. Mentions that the wicket played quite nicely but credits India for bowling well, saying it was not really free-flowing, you felt comfortable, but the scoreboard just was not going anywhere. He acknowledges that Kuldeep beat him in the drift and even jokes that he still can’t believe Kuldeep got him out, and on top of that, KL Rahul (both his teammates in the IPL), took the catch. Tristan stresses that first-innings runs are going to be crucial and hopes they can bat for as long as possible and extend the innings deep into Day 2.

On the other side of the break, Ryan Rickelton fell to Kuldeep Yadav after getting a solid start. South Africa rebuilt the innings through Temba Bavuma and Tristan Stubbs, who joined hands and did a pretty good job by adding 84 runs to the third wicket. Temba Bavuma fell while trying to clear the mid off region, while Tristan Stubbs departed one shy of his fifty. India rested their hopes on the spinners to do the job and Kuldeep Yadav and Ravindra Jadeja didn't disappoint as they claimed four wickets together.

So, the Test match started at a new destination as Guwahati kicked off its Test career. In the absence of Gill, Rishabh Pant became only the second wicket-keeper to lead India after the great MS Dhoni. Indian seamers, after being asked to bowl first, set the tone by bowling well with the new ball but around the 10th over or so, the pitch flattened out, allowing South Africa to grow into the game and start scoring. It was not until the final over before the end of the first session that Jasprit Bumrah crashed Aiden Markram's stumps.

So, it was a good day of cricket, but to highlight it on a big scale, the third session has put India on top as they picked 4 wickets. It was a good wicket to bat on, but a couple of the Proteas batters threw away their wickets. Tony de Zorzi and Senuran Muthusamy joined hands to get things back on track with a 45-run partnership, but Tony fell off the second new ball, at the stroke of Stumps.

The umpires want the light-meter as the visibility is not good enough. Okay, they have called it! STUMPS on Day 1! The light is not good enough. India would be reluctant to walk off as they had their tails up, while South Africa wouldn't mind as they were under pressure with the second new ball worrying them.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the third and final session of the day. The two umpires and players have made their way out to the middle. India are starting with spin in the form of Ravindra Jadeja. Tristan Stubbs to face. A slip and a short leg in place. Let's go...

With the ball softening as the day has progressed, batting has looked easier, and from South Africa’s perspective, it is now about building on the platform they have laid. As for India, they were a bit too defensive with their fields for the spinners in the morning, but were more attacking in the afternoon. That approach of limiting easy singles and forcing the batters to take risks appears to be the way forward. With the sun setting early in Guwahati, the light is expected to fade quickly, and it remains to be seen how much play will be possible in the final session. Join us back at 2 pm IST (8.30 am GMT) for the post-Lunch session. In the meantime, you can switch tabs and follow the Ashes action in Perth or the Bangladesh vs Ireland Test unfolding in Mirpur. Cheers!

What followed was a period of attritional batting from Temba Bavuma and Tristan Stubbs. Bavuma picked up where he left off in Kolkata, decisive with his footwork and assured in defence, while Stubbs, promoted to number three, showed commendable application against the spinners. Unlike Kolkata, where every ball felt like an event with sharp turn and variable bounce, the surface here has offered slower turn and far more predictability. Even so, take nothing away from the Proteas pair, who have applied themselves superbly so far. Jasprit Bumrah and Mohammed Siraj returned and operated in tandem as Rishabh Pant searched for a breakthrough. The duo got the ball to reverse and tested the South African pair with a stump-to-stump line, but the batters handled that phase with minimal discomfort.

SESSION SUMMARY - 28.1 overs, 74 runs and 1 wicket. A good session for South Africa. It was a session of rebuilding after the two openers perished on either side of the break, and it was a job well done by Tristan Stubbs and Temba Bavuma. The surface has settled down nicely, making it hard work for India’s bowlers, though they will take some encouragement from having kept the scoring rate in check. The hosts struck on the stroke of Tea and went into the break with a bit of momentum. Their spirits were lifted further when Kuldeep Yadav removed the other opener, Ryan Rickelton, immediately after the resumption.

Aiden Markram looked a bit rusty on his back foot as he edged three times onto the pads, and that determined Rishabh Pant to throw the ball towards Jasprit Bumrah for one final time before the break. As always, the master came up with a trick as he went past Aiden's inside edge, but this time onto the stumps. So, India wouldn't mind this start. They have contained South Africa from scoring free-flowing runs but they'll hope to be a bit more consistent with the ball. Join us back for the Post-Tea session at 11.30 am IST (5.50 am GMT).

The Indian seamers started well, beating the edge numerous times but Ryan Rickelton and Aiden Markram remained calm and took their time to score runs. Aiden Markram got off the mark on the 17th ball but got a big reprieve when KL Rahul dropped him on 4 at second slip. With the pitch flattening out a bit, Rishabh Pant turned to his spinners after the first hour. Washington Sundar and Kuldeep Yadav bowled in tandem, generating a lot of turn but no significant chances.

That's what he always does! Whenever India need a wicket, he comes up as if he has all the tricks in the world. He does have actually! So, South Africa go into the Tea losing Aiden Markram in the last over of the session. Apart from that, the visitors nailed every answer India threw at them. Win the toss, choose to bat first, and score runs in the first session. That's pretty good from the visitors, apart from that last over drama.

OUT! DRAGGED ON! Jasprit Bumrah has answered the skipper's call! Brought back for a 1 over burst before the Tea break, he has managed to break the opening stand. Aiden Markram throws his head back in disappointment. Pitched up with an upright seam, on off. Markram gets on the front foot and looks to firm the drive down the ground with a straight bat. The ball nips back in to catch the inside edge, and it crashes back onto the stumps. Aiden falls for 38 (81). The 82-run opening stand has been broken and that will be TEA on Day 1!

Commentary.Commentary: Time for the action to begin in Guwahati's Test debut. Devajit Saikia, the BCCI secretary, and BCCI president Mithun Manhas ring the bell to signal the start of play. India's 38th Test captain, Rishabh Pant, leads his men out onto the park. Aiden Markram and Ryan Rickelton will be the two openers for South Africa. Jasprit Bumrah will kickstart proceedings with the new ball. Bumrah to Markram. Three slips and a gully await. Here we go!

A giant circular banner featuring the badges of the BCCI and the Assam Cricket Association has been laid out in the centre. Devajit Saikia, the BCCI secretary, leads the way as the match officials and the two teams walk out for the national anthems. It will be South Africa’s national anthem first, followed by India’s.

South Africa (Playing XI) - Aiden Markram, Ryan Rickelton, Tristan Stubbs, Temba Bavuma (C), Tony de Zorzi, Wiaan Mulder, Senuran Muthusamy (In for Corbin Bosch), Kyle Verreynne (WK), Marco Jansen, Simon Harmer, Keshav Maharaj.

India (Playing XI) - KL Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Sai Sudharsan (In for Shubman Gill), Dhruv Jurel, Rishabh Pant (C/WK), Ravindra Jadeja, Nitish Kumar Reddy (In for Axar Patel), Washington Sundar, Kuldeep Yadav, Jasprit Bumrah, Mohammed Siraj.

India's skipper, Rishabh Pant says it is a proud moment to lead the country and he is thankful to the BCCI for giving him the opportunity, adding that he wants to grab it with both hands. Mentions the message to the group has been to focus on yourselves, look at the areas where you can improve, and fight for every moment out in the middle. Pant feels it is a good wicket, and bowling first is not a bad option. He adds that Shubman Gill is recovering and was eager to play, but his body did not allow it. Informs that Nitish Kumar Reddy comes in for Gill and Axar Patel misses out, with Sai Sudharsan replacing him.

The captain of South Africa, Temba Bavuma says they will bat first. Tells that they have to start fresh, feels the wicket looks a lot better, the boys are raring to go and put on a show for the next 4-5 days. Feels the wicket looks a lot better than it was in Kolkata, but reckons the fundamentals remain the same for them, they'll try and get a big score. Reckons the pitch is more consistent with not many cracks in it, and expects to play well in the first two days before the spin comes into play. Shares that it's a historic game and is happy to be a part of it. Informs that Senuran Muthusamy comes in for Corbin Bosch.
TOSS - Temba Bavuma calls it correctly and South Africa have elected to BAT first.

PITCH REPORT - Deep Dasgupta informs that it is a red soil wicket. Shaun Pollock adds that the track has a substantial grass covering, and he likes what he sees. Shaun says that he much prefers this pitch to the one in Kolkata. Believes that the fast bowlers should get something out of the new ball, especially with the early start and a bit of cloud cover around. Pollock expects some moisture to aid movement in the first hour, which could be challenging for the batters. He feels the captain winning the toss should bat first. Deep agrees, calling it a really good Test-match wicket, and with it being a red soil surface, he expects spin to come into play as the game progresses.

India’s recent struggles against spin have been well documented, with New Zealand exposing those frailties in 2024, and South Africa did the same in Kolkata. With Guwahati being an unknown quantity at the Test level, it only adds to the intrigue and drama surrounding what the 22 yards might have in store. Also remember, with daylight fading earlier in this part of the country, play will begin 30 minutes earlier than usual to maximise good light, with the Tea break taken first, followed by the Lunch interval. Stay tuned for the toss and team news.

India, once dominant at home, have now lost four of their last six Tests, and with their next home assignment only in 2027, they will be desperate to draw level in the series and collect crucial WTC points. The hosts will be without captain Shubman Gill, who has not recovered from the neck strain he suffered in Kolkata, meaning Rishabh Pant takes over the reins at a venue where he made his ODI debut. In Gill’s absence, added responsibility falls on Jaiswal, Rahul, and Pant. As always, India’s combination will be under the spotlight, especially the question of who replaces Gill.

South Africa created history in Kolkata with their first Test win in India in 15 years. Temba Bavuma’s gritty second-innings knock and Simon Harmer’s eight-wicket match haul led the way, even as lead spinner Keshav Maharaj was off colour. The tourists will again be without Kagiso Rabada, sidelined with a rib-bone stress injury, with Lungi Ngidi called in as cover. Chasing a first series win in India since 2000, the Proteas will hope for a stronger all-round batting effort to complement their in-form bowling unit.

Hello, one and all! We are here in Guwahati as the city gets ready to make its Test debut. The Barsapara Cricket Stadium will become India’s 30th Test venue, marking a historic moment for cricket in the region. The two-match series stands at 1-0 in favour of South Africa, who have carried their momentum from Pakistan into India and have played like the reigning Test champions. The pressure is firmly on India to respond and end the series on level terms.
